content.comment_body: Hello, this is my first time posting here. I hope to share knowledge and also receive help for my questions. Please excuse my English; it has been translated using Google. Here's my issue: I updated a project, replacing one [product_name] device with a different model to enable Modbus TCP communication. After making the changes, I exported the program from the earlier device to import it into the new one. The program loaded successfully, with a normal popup confirming conversion, and everything seems to work well on the device. However, the online monitoring mode doesn't show any variable states, even though the program runs fine. I have tried this on Windows 7 and Windows 10. Please, I hope the solution doesn't require rebuilding the project from scratch. Thanks!

Welcome to the forum. Simply loading a program created with [product_name] software version [version_no] using a newer version is only sufficient if the hardware remains the same. If your program was originally made for one hardware type, you must update the device selection in the software from the old hardware to the new model. If this step isn't done, you can transfer the program to the device, but online monitoring won't be available.
Hi, try updating the firmware of your [product_name] device to the latest hardware version first, then test again. Hope this resolves the issue.

Thanks for the help, the issue is resolved now. It was necessary to specify the correct hardware type in the device properties window, since it doesn't update automatically when selecting a new model in the network configuration. To explain: I exported a file from a project created with [product_name] software version [version_no] on one device, to import it into another. I updated the hardware type in the network window but not in the properties of the device itself; therefore, after importing, the program kept the previous device configuration. Hopefully this explanation is clear. Additionally, I updated the firmware to the latest version. Thanks to everyone for your input. (SPANISH) Muchas gracias por la ayuda, ha quedado solucionado. Era necesario especificar el tipo de hardware correcto en las propiedades del dispositivo, ya que no se actualiza automáticamente al cambiarlo en la configuración de red. Yo exporté el archivo desde un proyecto creado con la versión [version_no] en un dispositivo, para importarlo en otro. Actualicé el tipo de hardware en la ventana de red, pero no en las propiedades del propio dispositivo; por eso después de importar el programa seguía con la configuración anterior. Espero que se haya entendido la explicación. Además de esto he actualizado el firmware a la última versión. Gracias a todos por las aportaciones.
That was the issue, and it's now fixed. Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: The main issue occurred during project transfer between two different [product_name] hardware models using [product_name] software version [version_no]. While the program ran properly on the device, online monitoring failed to display variable states due to a mismatch in hardware configuration within the software. Updating the hardware type in both the network and device properties, along with a firmware update, resolved the problem. This situation emphasizes the need for clear workflow and synchronization when hardware changes occur, ensuring software settings reflect those modifications.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a smooth project migration process between various [product_name] hardware versions, including proper online monitoring and automatic propagation of hardware configuration changes within the software.
